title: The LLM bill is too high
brief: A 'summarize this product page' feature runs on 16 GPU replicas: $48/hr, and p99 is about 11 s. Finance wants the bill cut by more than half, without making users wait longer. Find where the money goes, then cut it.

requirements: 70% are for the same popular products: an answer cache can hit at most 0.7
variants.twist: Product pages change hourly, so the cache TTL drops and the hit ratio falls to 0.4 (set hit_ratio 0.4). What does that cost?

requirements: 40 requests/s, all unique: no cache helps
Summaries can arrive a few minutes later by notification: the request only has to be accepted
variants.twist: Launch day doubles requests for a while: spike(multiplier=2, seconds=30). Let the backlog grow, or add GPUs? What's the cost of each?

hints: Why does a GPU pool serving waiting users have to sit mostly idle? Which requests didn't need a GPU at all?
Repeated prompts can be answered from a cache. If nobody waits for the answer, a queue lets the GPUs run near 80% busy instead of about 45%.
Repeats: cache (hit 0.7) in front of the LLM, about 6 replicas. Async: service -> queue -> worker -> LLM with about 9 replicas; the service only enqueues.
_notes: Starter: client (timeout 60 s) -> LB -> 2 services (timeout 60 s) -> LLM x16: rho 0.5, p99 ~11.3 s, $48.23. Repeats: cache 0.7 -> LLM sees 12/s. 5 replicas: p99 ~8.4 s, $15.38; 6: ~6.7 s, $18.38; 7 ($21.38) breaks the budget. Async: service -> queue -> 1 worker -> LLM. 9 replicas (rho 0.89): p99 38 ms, $27.38; 7 replicas fall behind (backlog grows ~5/s); 10 ($30.38) break the budget. Also worth raising: smaller model, shorter prompts, batching. Cost per token isn't modeled; the sim prices GPU-hours. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
